fixes.explanation: The altar is on Moses' mind earlier in the passage, so I get it, baker. But when he and the Levitical priests speak to all Israel, the first word is “Be silent, O Israel, and listen!” (Deuteronomy 27:9). The verse opens with listening. It doesn't send the crowd anywhere.

That's right, baker. Moses says these tribes are to stand on Mount Gerizim “…to bless the people…” (Deuteronomy 27:12). He names six: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin. Not a bad assignment to get.

That's it, baker. Moses says, “Write on them all the words of this law when you have crossed over to enter the land…” (Deuteronomy 27:3). Not a few favorites, not a highlights reel. ALL the words of this law, on big plastered stones.

You've got it, baker. Moses says, “You must not use any iron tool on them.” (Deuteronomy 27:5). Then he repeats it: the altar of the LORD goes up with uncut stones (Deuteronomy 27:6). So no iron tools on those stones. They go up just as they are.

That's the word, baker. The curse says, “Cursed is he who moves his neighbor’s boundary stone.” (Deuteronomy 27:17). A boundary stone marks where a neighbor's land is. Moving it is the thing that gets named. And all the people say, “Amen!”

Fixing things sounds like a friendly act, so I see the pull, friend. But the curse says, “Cursed is he who moves his neighbor’s boundary stone.” (Deuteronomy 27:17). The word in the verse is moves, not repairs.

That's right, baker. The curse says, “Cursed is he who lets a blind man wander in the road.” (Deuteronomy 27:18). Look at the wording. It's about letting him wander. The curse names the one who lets it happen.

Yes, baker. The curse says, “Cursed is he who withholds justice from the foreigner, the fatherless, or the widow.” (Deuteronomy 27:19). Three groups get named: the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow. Justice is what's held back from them. And all the people say, “Amen!”
